title: Detect Squares
description: Design a structure that adds 2D points (duplicates allowed) and, given a query point, counts the ways to choose three stored points that form an axis-aligned square with positive area together with the query point.

reference.use_case: Storing a stream of points and quickly counting how many axis-aligned squares a new point would complete with previously seen points.
system_examples: Document and UI analysis — recovering axis-aligned boxes such as table cells from detected corner points
CAD and surveying tools — recognizing square plots or grid cells from measured points
reference.explanation: Counting point frequencies in a hash map lets each query try every stored point as the diagonal corner and look up the other two corners in O(1), giving O(n) per query instead of O(n³). It is mainly a design exercise in choosing an index that turns geometric search into counted lookups.
